excerpt: Step-by-step managed processes to let your agent handle incorporating, hiring, payroll, and more.
Start a process in one agent and finish it in another, on your laptop or your phone.
Move to a new model the day it ships. Your company and work in progress come with you.
Ultrametric runs no model. The work uses the AI plan you already pay for.
In your agent host's remote MCP settings, add a connection with this server URL: https://api.ultrametric.ai/mcp
npm install -g ultrametric@0.4.1
With `--json`, the agent gets the link and controls completion without an interactive prompt.
ultrametric init --dry-run --json ... The first command previews changes. The second writes the selected skill files.
You can commit the skill files to share the setup with your team.
Page through the catalog and retrieve the instructions your agent needs.
To select a specific version, replace `VERSION` with its positive integer version number
adapters accept `--path` to add local project context and a template to the guide response. That context stays local during retrieval.
Keep decisions, documents, and process progress for the next session.
Use `--period` when a recurring process needs a separate run for a particular period.
Find a saved company, run, or record in a new agent session.
For history, select one record or run: ultrametric context get --record RECORD_ID --history --json
An update to an existing record must include its current revision so one session does not overwrite another session's changes.
If a save times out, retry the exact input with the same update key.
Both connections use the same process service and hosted company records. Sign in to the same account and organization to continue work across them.
Read process guides and work with company context over HTTP.
download the [OpenAPI contract](/contracts/openapi.json) for request and response schemas
Use `--json` when an agent runs the CLI. Successful results appear on stdout as a `schemaVersion` and `data` object.
The `--environment` option accepts `production` or `staging`.
`doctor` reports the CLI version, selected API origin, and local file locations.
Read protected context | Also `context:protected:read`
ask the agent to call MCP `status` with its `processId`. The result includes `releaseAccess` and `available`.

Recorded keyless CLI sweep (2026-10-07, docs/self-eval-probes/transcript-self-eval-keyless.txt): `$ npx -y ultrametric@0.4.1 --version` → `0.4.1` (exit 0). Every command `ultrametric --help` enumerates was run keylessly in a scratch --data-dir; `doctor` printed version, Node, storage/auth/settings/log paths, and API endpoints, and `logs show` printed per-command diagnostics (name, exit code, duration).

Recorded keyless probe (2026-10-07): `$ ultrametric init --path <scratch> --dry-run` → 'Initialization preview: … create: …/project/.agents/skills/ultrametric/SKILL.md / create: …/project/.claude/skills/ultrametric/SKILL.md' (exit 0) — the dry run previews both harness targets (Codex .agents/skills and Claude Code .claude/skills) without writing anything.

Recorded keyless probe (2026-10-07): `$ ultrametric auth login --json` → {"status": "pending", "loginId": "9bccf821-…", "userCode": "KHFW-RQVS", "verificationUri": "https://api.ultrametric.ai/auth/login", "verificationUriComplete": "…?user_code=KHFW-RQVS", "expiresAt": …, "retryAfter": 5} (exit 0); `auth complete <login-id>` printed the verification URI, code, expiry, and retry guidance (exit 0). A device-code login an agent can drive end to end up to the human approval step; the recorded code expired minutes later, unapproved.

Recorded keyless refusals (2026-10-07): `$ ultrametric process list` → 'Error [AUTH_REQUIRED]: API login is required.' (exit 1); `process get` and `process open` refuse identically; `$ context get --json` → {"schemaVersion":1,"error":{"code":"AUTH_REQUIRED","message":"API login is required.","hint":"Run ultrametric auth login."}} (exit 1). Every process-shaped function requires login: a keyless visitor cannot retrieve or run a single hosted guide.

Recorded keyless MCP probe (2026-10-07): POST https://api.ultrametric.ai/mcp `initialize` → HTTP/2 401, body {"schemaVersion":1,"error":{"code":"AUTH_REQUIRED","message":"Sign in to continue."}}; `tools/list` → the same AUTH_REQUIRED body. Headers carry `www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://api.ultrametric.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"` and that well-known document answers 200 with {"resource":"https://api.ultrametric.ai/mcp","authorization_servers":["https://auth.ultrametric.ai"],…}. The hosted MCP refuses even the keyless initialize handshake; the wall carries the full RFC 9728 pattern (401 + resource metadata + live well-known document).

Recorded keyless probe (2026-10-07): `$ ultrametric understand --json` → a complete company-profile guide (kind "company_profile_guide": instructions, template, result schema, agent-trial spec), offline, exit 0; `$ assess --json` → a complete four-dimension AI-readiness assessment (rubric, readiness levels, steps, template, result schema), offline, exit 0. The largest keyless payloads the CLI ships: real, usable guide content with no account.

Recorded keyless probe (2026-10-07): `$ ultrametric companies validate --file empty-profile.json` → 'Error [VALIDATION]: Input does not match the required schema.' with per-field errors naming each violation (schemaVersion, operation, companyId, asOf, facts, review, nextSteps), offline, exit 3; `companies schema` / `assessments schema` print the full JSON Schemas with worked examples, and `actions set` rejects a bad --status by enumerating the allowed states (proposed, planned, in_progress, done, dismissed). Local, revisioned, schema-enforced record stores working without any hosted dependency.

Recorded keyless probe (2026-10-07): `$ ultrametric context schema open` / `save` / `get` → the hosted API's full input schemas (JSON Schema 2020-12) printed with no login (exit 0). The hosted API's input contracts are readable before sign-in; the hosted `context get`/`save` operations behind them require login.

At the 2026-10-07 recording all four `arena` commands failed keylessly: `$ ultrametric arena categories --json` → {"schemaVersion":1,"error":{"code":"NETWORK_ERROR","message":"Could not reach ProductArena.","hint":"Check your connection and retry."}} (exit 1) — the shipped CLI fetched a redirecting data path (docs/SELF-EVAL.md, Broken). Re-verified 2026-10-08 after the worker fix deployed: https://ultrametric.ai/productarena/data/categories.json answers HTTP/2 200 (application/json) and `npx -y ultrametric@0.4.1 arena categories --json` prints the arena catalog (exit 0).
